dependencies.reason: is served by the same service and must run on both of its deployment targets
shares the OAuth provider its sign-in uses, and identifies the same user, without using the API key route
reads its workspaces and inherits its access decision through the API
reads the patch list and the rebuilds the workspace view shows
reads the merge jobs the workspace view shows
reads the recent events the workspace view shows

tasks.title: Choose the front-end tooling and lay down the design tokens
steps: Choose the front-end framework, the build, the session mechanism and the accessibility and contrast testing tools, verify each against its installed types, and record the choices in an ADR
Add this task's behaviours to the design system test file, and confirm they fail
Define the design tokens once — type scale, spacing, status colours and the dark and light palettes — in the visual language of GitHub and GitHub Copilot
Build the three shared patterns the pages use: the repository list, the status badge and the timeline
Forbid hard-coded type and spacing values in page styles, so every page draws from the tokens
Confirm the web interface builds and is served by both deployment targets of package 01

tasks.title: Serve the landing page
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the landing page test files, and confirm they fail
Serve a landing page saying what the service is and what it does, with a sign-in control leading to the provider
Serve it to a visitor with no session, including at the addresses of the dashboard and a workspace view
Confirm by test that no page served without a session carries a workspace slug, a user name, an organization name or a count of them

tasks.title: Sign a person in without touching their API keys
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the web session test files, and confirm they fail
Implement the browser sign-in against the same OAuth provider the API uses, establishing a session that identifies the same user
Do not call the API's callback route, and neither issue nor revoke an API key, so a key the person's automation holds keeps working
Carry the session so that another site cannot make a request with it, give it a lifetime, and end it on sign-out
Show the landing page, not an error, to a visitor with no session or with one that has expired or been signed out

tasks.title: Read everything through the API as the signed-in person
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the web reads test files, and confirm they fail
Make every page read through the service's own API as the signed-in person, with no direct access to the relational store or the repository store
Show one indistinguishable not-available page for a workspace the person may not read, one that is archived and invisible to them, and an address naming nothing, revealing no field of any of them
Show a member exactly what the API returns a member, omitting every section the API would refuse them

tasks.title: Show the dashboard
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the dashboard test files, and confirm they fail
List the signed-in person's workspaces with slug, status, their access and last sync, each linking to that workspace's view
Show a never-synced workspace as not yet synced rather than as an empty cell
Confirm by test that the set of workspaces shown equals the set the API returns for the same person
Show a person with no workspaces a message saying so and what to do next

tasks.title: Show one workspace's state
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the workspace view test files, and confirm they fail
Show the workspace's slug, display name, description, status, mode, head, upstream head, last sync, settings and any clone or sync error, omitting an error that is null

Show a carry_patch workspace's patches in position order with position, branch, status and latest rebuild result, and the latest rebuild or a statement that none has run, showing no patch section for a standard workspace
Show the workspace's most recent jobs and most recent events, newest first, each with its kind and time
Render each section independently, so a failing read leaves the rest of the page usable and names what could not be read

tasks.title: Make every page themed, responsive, keyboard-operable and Parley's own
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the theming, responsive, accessibility and branding test files, and confirm they fail
Provide a dark and a light theme following the viewer's system setting, overridable and remembered across a reload
Confirm by measurement that every text and background pair meets the contrast level for normal text in both themes
Make every page render at a viewport 360 pixels wide with no horizontal scrolling and no clipped or overlapping content, with long slugs and descriptions wrapping

Make every link, button and control reachable in a sensible keyboard order with a visible focus indicator, give each page one main landmark and a heading structure with no skipped level, and give every control an accessible name
Carry Parley's name and marks on every page, and use no GitHub name, logo or wordmark as the site's identity

tasks.title: Drive a real browser against a running deployment
steps: Add the three smoke tests and confirm each passes against a running deployment with a real browser, or skips with a message naming what was missing

Trace 15-PATH-1: the sign-in reaches the stub provider, establishes a session through the web auth route, and the dashboard reads through the API as that person, while the API key held throughout is still accepted
Trace 15-PATH-2: the workspace view's sections each read their own API route as the signed-in person, and the values rendered match those responses
Trace 15-PATH-3: the dashboard's list and the not-available page both come from the access decision of package 03 through the API, with no separate rule in the web layer

For every criterion carrying a contract, confirm a caller in production code consumes the producer's result and not only a test: the design tokens are used by every page, the API client by every read, and the session by every page behind sign-in
Confirm the web interface is served by both deployment targets of package 01, so the portability claim covers it
Grep web/ and the files every task's touches lists for TODO, FIXME and the project's not-implemented marker, and remove any that remain
Add the web interface conformance cases to the harness from package 01
done_when: `make check` passes with no network access and no deployment configured
a real browser signs in, reads the dashboard and opens a workspace against a running deployment
the contrast, responsive and keyboard checks pass for every page in both themes
